assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work transformed empirical understanding of how technology, trade exposure and changing task demand reshape employment and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are central to the integrated task and trade-shock evidence; the three-person limit leaves important adjacent contributors outside.
assessment.maturity: Its principal findings have been extensively tested, replicated and incorporated into research and public-policy analysis over many years.
uncertainties: The contribution combines several related literatures, making the most defensible division of credit difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification made transparent inference possible when strong identifying assumptions cannot be justified, with broad consequences for applied economics.
assessment.attribution: Manski supplied the foundational framework, while Tamer and Molinari made major contributions to moment-inequality identification and inference.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are longstanding, technically well developed and widely used across empirical fields.
uncertainties: The cited set spans foundational and later contributions whose relative priority is not fully resolved here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony changed how economists interpret wages, employer power and labor-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the clearest central contributor to the modern monopsony framework; other named researchers have important but less singular links to the stated discovery.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a substantial empirical literature and is highly consequential for contemporary labor-market analysis.
uncertainties: Empirical estimates of labor-market power and the appropriate scope of policy implications remain contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence and audit studies provided unusually direct evidence on labor-market discrimination and reshaped empirical work on unequal treatment.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are particularly associated with the canonical modern correspondence-study contribution; credit across the broader audit tradition is necessarily incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The design has been repeatedly applied in multiple settings and remains a durable benchmark for discrimination research.
uncertainties: External validity and the mapping from callback discrimination to wider labor-market outcomes require care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data radically improved measurement of intergenerational mobility and revealed the importance of place for economic opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central architects of the mobility and place-based program, with Friedman a major collaborator on the underlying linked-data research.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has already had major scholarly and policy influence, though parts of the causal interpretation remain actively developed.
uncertainties: The program is comparatively recent, and mechanisms behind geographic mobility differences are not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made forward-looking behavioral models empirically operational in labor, industrial organization and related fields.
assessment.attribution: Rust supplied the seminal breakthrough, while Keane and Eckstein made influential extensions and applications within the stated research program.
assessment.maturity: This is a mature and highly influential methodological tradition with decades of use.
uncertainties: The field includes many further contributors, and structural conclusions can remain sensitive to modeling choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM gave empirical economists practical tools to address persistent unobserved heterogeneity and endogeneity in short panels.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond form a coherent core for the principal estimators and their development.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding, foundational in applied work and thoroughly studied.
uncertainties: Routine application can be fragile when instruments proliferate or identifying assumptions are weak.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life health and skill formation established that childhood conditions can have enduring economic consequences.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are key empirical contributors, while Cunha is central to the dynamic human-capital framework that organizes this evidence.
assessment.maturity: A broad literature now supports the importance of early conditions, with substantial influence on education and health policy.
uncertainties: Evidence spans heterogeneous interventions and mechanisms, so a single unified discovery is less sharply delimited.
